usdRate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 6 (BD exchange rates against selected currencies)
usdRate.note: The dinar is pegged at 0.376 per US dollar, unchanged in every period of the table; World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2025 also 0.376. CLDR gives no narrow symbol; 'BD' is the usual local abbreviation.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics, citing the Information & eGovernment Authority (iGA), CPI September 2026
inflation_cpi.note: Consumer prices up 3.1% year on year in September 2026 (3.0% in August); secondary source because the iGA release could not be read. World Bank 2025 average -0.1%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: World Bank CPI inflation 2021-2025 (about 1% average); latest 3.1% (September 2026); dollar peg
inflation_projection.note: With the dinar pegged to the dollar, inflation has averaged about 1% over 2021-2025 and is 3.1% now, so 2% a year is used for long-range plans.

policy_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain press release, 28 October 2026: overnight deposit rate unchanged
policy_rate.note: The CBB kept its overnight deposit rate, its key policy rate, unchanged at 4.50%. Its August 2026 bulletin shows the average repo rate at 5.25% in Q2 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 7 (conventional retail banks, BD savings deposits)
savings_account_rate.note: Average rate on BD savings deposits at conventional retail banks, 0.18% in August 2026.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 7 (BD time deposits, 3-6 months)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average rate on BD time deposits of 3-6 months, 2.69% in August 2026 (less than 3 months: 2.67%); deposits in the BD 10,000-50,000 range.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 7 (BD time deposits, 6-12 months)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average rate on BD time deposits of 6-12 months, 2.64% in August 2026; deposits in the BD 10,000-50,000 range.

dps_rate.note: No industry-wide rate for a monthly recurring deposit product was found in the CBB statistics.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, banking indicators (average interest rate on deposits, 6-12 months)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Quarterly average rate on 6-12 month deposits, 2.63% in Q2 2026 (2.00% in Q1); no weighted average over all deposits is published. World Bank FR.INR.DPST stops in 2015.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond for individuals was found; government securities are auctioned to banks and institutions through the CBB.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 11 (Government of Bahrain Treasury Bills)
tbill_91d_rate.note: Average rate on the weekly 91-day bills allotted on 26 August 2026 (BD 70 million at a price of 98.684); recent auctions ranged 5.28-5.48%.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year government bond yield is published; the CBB bulletin gives only the average yield on long-term development bonds.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, banking indicators (average interest rate on local and international long-term government bonds)
tbond_10y_rate.note: Average yield on long-term government development bonds, 6.69% in Q2 2026 (5.96% in Q1); maturities are not split out, so this is used as the long bond yield.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Bahrain, taxes on personal income
tax_bank_interest.note: There is no personal income tax in Bahrain, so bank interest is untaxed for individuals.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Bahrain, taxes on personal income
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No personal income tax, so returns on government securities are untaxed for individuals (no retail savings certificate exists).

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Consumer information: Deposit & URIA Protection Scheme
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Eligible individual account holders are covered up to BD 20,000 of their total eligible accounts per bank (conventional deposits and Islamic unrestricted investment accounts), replacing the earlier lower of 75% or BD 15,000.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026, Table 7 (conventional retail banks, credit cards)
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Average interest rate on credit card balances at conventional retail banks, 20.77% in August 2026; no legal cap was found.

equity_return_low.note: Low case: the local market, dominated by a few banks, returns less than Treasury bills.

equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 2 points above the Treasury bill yield, within the 4-point cap, because the Bahrain All Share index has had only a moderate, dividend-driven 10-year record.

equity_return_high.note: High case: a stronger equity premium similar to other Gulf markets.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Dollar peg (0.376 BHD per USD); World Bank exchange rate
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold; the peg means no currency boost.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Dollar peg (0.376 BHD per USD); long-run dollar gold trend
gold_return_base.note: Base case: the long-run dollar gold trend of about 4% a year, with no depreciation gain under the peg.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Dollar peg (0.376 BHD per USD); long-run dollar gold trend
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold years.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (deposit rates)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall back toward the 2025 level of about 1.9%, untaxed.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (1-year deposit 2.64%)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: the 6-12 month deposit rate, untaxed; Treasury bills pay more but are bid for by banks and institutions.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (Treasury bills 5.28%, policy rate 4.5%)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: savers who reach Treasury bill or sukuk returns through banks or funds.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The CBB (the insurance regulator) publishes no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold, but no published premium rates per BD 1,000 of cover by age were found from the regulator or another public source.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No published private health insurance premiums by age were found from a public source.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Bahrain
oop_health_share.note: 28.7% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database via the World Bank); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.note: No medical CPI was read; private medical costs usually rise about 2 points faster than general prices.

goal_inflation_education.note: No education CPI was read; private school fees usually rise faster than general prices, so 2 points above the inflation assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Bahrain
life_expectancy.note: 81.4 years in 2024 (men 80.9, women 82.1); the population includes many younger migrant workers.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 5.18 (2025, World Bank), 8.7 (2040) and 15.0 (2065, populationpyramid.net/bahrain/2065/); the large migrant workforce keeps the ratio high.

retirement_age_default.note: The Social Insurance Organization site and the social insurance law could not be read (access refused), so the current private-sector pension age could not be confirmed.

retirement_age_government.note: The civil-service pension age could not be confirmed; the Social Insurance Organization site could not be read.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (deposit rates)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates near their 2025 level, untaxed.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (1-year deposit 2.64%)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: the untaxed 6-12 month deposit rate; not above the after-tax 1-year deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (Treasury bills 5.28%)
retirement_return_high.note: High case: part of the money earns Treasury bill or sukuk returns.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026 (deposits and Treasury bills)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a mix earning a little above deposit rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026; equity base 7.5%; gold base 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of deposits or sukuk, equities and some gold.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Bahrain, Monthly Statistical Bulletin, August 2026; equity high 10%

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Means-tested social assistance from the Ministry of Social Development covers some older people, but no current amount of an old-age allowance could be read from an official source.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Eligibility rules for social assistance to older people could not be read from an official source.

gratuity_rule.note: The National Portal says the Labour Law gives expatriate employees a statutory end-of-service indemnity (Bahraini nationals are covered by social insurance instead), but the Labour Law text giving the days per year could not be opened (access refused).

public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory social insurance through the Social Insurance Organization covers Bahraini public and private employees (the National Portal says a full pension needs 20 years of insured employment and is based on the last five years' average pay), but the pension age and indexation rules could not be read.

savings_account.note: Savings accounts pay very little (0.18% on average in August 2026).

fdr_3m.note: Deposits are protected up to BD 20,000 per person per bank.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product was found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals was found.

tbill_91d.note: 91-day bills are auctioned weekly by the CBB to eligible institutions; individuals can take part through their retail banks or Bahrain Bourse. Al Salam sukuk are also issued monthly.

tbond_5y.note: Issued in dinars and US dollars, mainly bought by institutions.

tbond_10y.note: Issued in dinars and US dollars, mainly bought by institutions.

equity_fund.note: The CBB bulletin counts 1,683 mutual funds registered in Bahrain in Q2 2026, with USD 11.5 billion invested.

gold.note: Gold bars, coins and jewellery are freely sold.

insuranceRegulator.name: Central Bank of Bahrain, insurance supervision

insuranceComplaints.name: Central Bank of Bahrain, consumer complaints

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Health (public health care for citizens)

depositInsurance.name: Deposit & Unrestricted Investment Accounts Protection Scheme, Central Bank of Bahrain
